subject.title: feat(codex): config to disable or scope the native hook relay (#91009)

question: Should the bundled Codex plugin support an operator configuration that disables every native relay callback, including PermissionRequest, or must approval-critical events remain enforced when the approval policy is active?
rationale: The implementation is mechanically narrow and its live proof is positive, but choosing whether a resource-mitigation switch may disable approval/policy callbacks is a product and security-boundary decision that code review cannot infer.

options.title: Preserve approval-critical relays
options.body: Allow event scoping for performance control but retain permission_request whenever the active approval policy needs native approval handling.

options.title: Approve an explicit emergency bypass
options.body: Allow enabled:false to clear all native callbacks, but document it as a deliberate advanced policy bypass and add coverage for the approval-disabled consequence.

options.title: Defer the new control
options.body: Land or prioritize the narrower idle-PreToolUse behavior first and postpone broad operator relay policy until its security contract is agreed.

recommendation.title: Preserve approval-critical relays
recommendation.body: Allow event scoping for performance control but retain permission_request whenever the active approval policy needs native approval handling.

likelyOwner.reason: Their active adjacent work changes the same Codex native-hook registration boundary and is the closest evidence-backed routing candidate available from the supplied history.
